title: mapwright: name, repo and first maps

questions.title: Plugin name
questions.question: What should the mapmaking plugin be called?
questions.background: Working name is mapwright. Evergreen already owns 'map this repo' (codemaps), so the word map may pull code prompts toward it.
questions.why: The name goes into the repo, skill names and trigger descriptions; changing it after release is costly.

guess.why: Plain and findable; the trigger evals will include codemap decoys to keep the prompts apart.

questions.title: Public or private
questions.question: Should the repository start public or private?
questions.background: Most sibling plugins (polywright, fractalwright) went public at their first release.
questions.why: Decides whether research and test maps must be checked for licences before the first push.

options.label: Private until the first release, then public

guess.why: Same path as the other wright plugins.

questions.title: First three maps
questions.question: Which of your projects should get the first life-like, fantasy and sci-fi maps?
questions.background: Step E makes one keeper map per kind before release.
questions.why: These become the plugin's first real uses and its tests.

guess.text: Life-like: a real place you name (not home). Fantasy: a region for a story or the Starfinder game. Sci-fi: a sector map from UniverseGenerator output.

questions.title: AI styling
questions.question: How much should maps lean on AI image styling?
questions.background: Image models garble labels and move rivers; the plan draws geometry in code, then optionally restyles it with a control image and sets labels afterwards.
questions.why: Decides whether aistyle is built early or left last.

options.label: Code render by default, AI pass optional
AI pass on most fantasy maps

guess.why: Keeps every map checkable; the AI pass is extra polish.

questions.title: Keyed services
questions.question: May the plugin use any keyed or paid map services?
questions.background: Open data (OpenStreetMap, Natural Earth, Copernicus DEM, Gaia) covers most needs. Mapbox, MapTiler and Google need keys and have strict terms.
questions.why: Decides whether find/fetch ever asks for an API key.

options.label: Free-tier keys allowed, I will set them up

guess.why: No accounts, no bills, simpler licences.

questions.title: Scout engagement
questions.question: Should the mapmaking everscout beat stay read-only?
questions.background: Many hand-drawn map communities ban or dislike AI art.
questions.why: Read-only means no drafted comments to makers on that beat.

options.label: Ask makers where the community's rules allow it

guess.why: Low risk; can open up later.
